title: Ingrown toenail | NHS inform
text:
Ingrown toenail
An ingrown toenail is a common problem where the nail grows into the skin around the nail. It can be painful but there are ways to manage the discomfort.
Symptoms of an ingrown toenail
An ingrown toenail usually affects the big toe, but it can happen on any toe.
The nail may curl into the toe. The skin around the toe can also become red, swollen and tender.
An ingrown toenail most often affects the big toe.
An ingrown toenail can cause pain, swelling and redness. Sometimes it may become infected.
Signs of infection
Sometimes an ingrown toenail can become infected. This may:
cause pus to come out of the area
make you to feel hot and shivery
Treatment for an ingrown toenail
If you have an ingrown toenail, there are some things you can try at home to help.
Do
soak your foot in warm, salty water – this helps to soften the skin around the toe and reduces the chance of infection
dry your feet well after washing them
wear wide, comfortable shoes or sandals
take
paracetamol
or
ibuprofen
to reduce pain
Don’t
do not cut your toenail – leave it to grow out
do not pick at your toe or toenail
do not wear tight, pointy shoes
Get help from a pharmacist
If you have an ingrown toenail, you can ask a pharmacist about:
treatments to help ease the pain and prevent an infection
whether you need to see a GP
Speak to your GP practice if:
treating your ingrown toenail at home is not helping
your toe is painful and swollen with pus coming out of it
you have a very high temperature or you feel hot or shivery
you have diabetes and an ingrown toenail – foot problems can be more serious if you have diabetes
Treatment from a GP practice
If you think you have an ingrown toenail, your GP practice may:
check your symptoms
give you antibiotics if you have an infection
If you have a badly ingrown toenail, your GP practice may refer you to a foot specialist (podiatrist).
Treatment from a foot specialist
A foot specialist may:
cut away part of the nail
remove the whole nail
You may have a local anaesthetic to numb your toe when this is done.
What causes an ingrown toenail?
Some things that may contribute to an ingrown toenail include:
not cutting the toenails well
wearing tight shoes, socks or tights
having sweaty feet
an injury
the shape of the nail
a fungal nail infection
How to prevent an ingrown toenail
To help prevent an ingrown toenail, it can help to:
cut your toenails straight across the top and not right to the edges
wear comfortable shoes that fit properly – make sure they’re not too tight
keep your feet clean
dry your feet well after washing
avoid cutting your toenails very short
